chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abi al-Hasan al-Sa'i, from Burayd, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام: concerning

A man who accuses a group of people altogether with a single word—he عليه السلام said regarding him: “If he did not name them, then only one hadd is upon him; and if he named them, then for each man one hadd is upon him.”

key_terms.الْقَوْمَ: the group of people being accused
key_terms.بِكَلِمَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ: with a single statement or expression
key_terms.لَمْ يُسَمِّهِمْ: he did not identify them by name
key_terms.لِكُلِّ رَجُلٍ حَدٌّ: for each individual man there is a separate prescribed punishment
key_terms.يَقْذِفُ: he accuses falsely, particularly with slanderous imputation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone falsely accuses an entire group with one statement?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on false accusation against multiple people. If a person slanders a group collectively without naming individuals, one hadd applies; but if he names them individually, a separate hadd applies for each person.
